Which platform/qemu instance was this tested on?
This was tested on one of the NVIDIA platforms

The only upstream platform is gb200nvl-obmc.  I'm assuming you tested on that, but considering that doesn't enable bios yet, I'm not sure how you tested.

Please make sure you're testing upstream, and not uploading a patch to a downstream platform.

I tested the patch on romulus qemu environment. I enabled `biosconfig-manager` recipe. 
The test failed as in the qemu environment there was no json file which stores password(https://github.com/openbmc/bios-settings-mgr/blob/master/include/password.hpp#L34)
```
root@romulus:~#
root@romulus:~# ls /var/lib/bios-settings-manager/
root@romulus:~#
```
Updated the commit message to reflect the proper testing procedure

> The test failed as in the qemu environment there was no json file which stores password

This is what I would've expected.

I transferred the required files to romulus qemu and performed the test. 
But it shall be only updated in the BMC and we wont be able to send the password to BIOS as in qemu platform that is not possible.

> I transferred the required files to romulus qemu and performed the test.

So put that in a patch for meta-gb200?

> we wont be able to send the password to BIOS as in qemu platform that is not possible.

This is kind of my point.  There's no way to test this, and it's missing all the infrastructure to ever work.

Please use gb200nvl-obmc target to build on your machine.  Send patches to openbmc/openbmc/meta-nvidia/meta-gb200-obmc for the config entries you need.

Marking the conversation resolved. If there is any suggestions on testing please let me know I will perform

?  I’m not sure how it could work as is.  there’s no connection to bios at the moment.  please verify that you tested that bios actually applied the password.  how does bios settings manager pass the password to bios on gb200 if the pldm handlers aren’t configured upstream?

On NVIDIA platforms the support for pldm for bios configuration doesnt exists. IPMI OEM commands are used to transfer BIOS password on the next boot. 
The testing on current patch is limited to change in dbus values.

where are those  oem commands in review?  and where is the patch to enable them on gb200?  the whole feature needs to work to pass the test.

I’m here to help you, but I need to know what you need help with.

I agree that enabling upstream support for NVIDIA IPMI OEM commands is necessary for this feature. For reference, the relevant OEM commands are documented here: https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-ipmi-oem.

However, I wanted to clarify that even with this support enabled, we currently cannot emulate the BIOS sending these commands. Given this limitation, could we consider treating this patch as independent of full BIOS integration, so that upstream enablement is not blocked? Please let me know if this approach aligns with our testing and integration plans.

> I agree that enabling upstream support for NVIDIA IPMI OEM commands is necessary for this feature. For reference, the relevant OEM commands are documented here: https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-ipmi-oem.

Yep, and that's Nvidia private github.  That code needs to make it upstream.

> 
> However, I wanted to clarify that even with this support enabled, we currently cannot emulate the BIOS sending these commands.

No need to emulate.  We have gb200 systems that can load upstream builds.

> Given this limitation, could we consider treating this patch as independent of full BIOS integration, so that upstream enablement is not blocked? Please let me know if this approach aligns with our testing and integration plans.

It does not align unfortunately.  The feature needs to work in testing as a user would see it, including all backends.  Otherwise, there's no real point to enabling it, and it's just dead code.  If all the backends to make it work are in process and in review, that's fine, but ipmi is going to be a prereq here.
What happens on a system that doesn't support this?

We will expose the Action URI to perform password change. 
If the backend service is not running it needs to be taken care gracefully when dbus error occurs
I updated the patch set, we will first check the existence of dbus object path("/xyz/openbmc_project/bios_config/password") and then only formulate the URI to perform password change
